- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to compensate.
- After a sharp price spike (≥2% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +1.5% above peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.3 to -1.0 within 3 days), model fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast by 0.3–0.8% per day toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts in early periods when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; reduce first 5–7 forecast values by 0.5–1.0%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +1.3/1.4 values, model tends to overreact; apply downward bias of 0.7–1.2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
